note: Super Login alters the core login/registration/password-reset forms via hook_form_alter, driven entirely by the config object super_login.settings whose values are nested under a super_login.* key (read as super_login.settings -> super_login.<key>). Configure route super_login.settings (/admin/config/people/super_login/settings), core 'administer site configuration' permission, no own permission/Drush/plugins. Login Type: 0 username-or-email, 1 username-only, 2 email-only (implemented by super_login_user_login_validate swapping an email for the account's username). Cases are grounded in these real keys; medium/hard scripts set and read login_type, capslock, autofocus and restore shipped defaults explicitly.

evals.prompt: Using the Super Login module, how do I let people sign in to my Drupal site with their email address only? Name the setting and the value.
evals.expected_output: Set Login Type (config super_login.settings -> super_login.login_type) to 2 for email-only. 0 = username or email, 1 = username only, 2 = email only. A validate handler looks up the account by email and substitutes the real username before core authenticates.

evals.prompt: Where does the Super Login module store its settings, and what is the peculiarity of the key path when reading a single value like the login type with drush?
evals.expected_output: Settings live in the config object super_login.settings, but every value is nested under a super_login key, so a value is read as super_login.settings -> super_login.<key>, e.g. drush cget super_login.settings super_login.login_type.

evals.prompt: What does the Super Login module add to or change on the core user login form?
evals.expected_output: It relabels the username field, adds a Forgot password? link and a Create new account link, an optional Caps Lock warning, field placeholders, optional autofocus, widens the inputs, can move status messages outside the form, and removes the login/register/reset tabs.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, which login identifiers does Super Login currently accept (username, email, or both)? Inspect the live configuration to answer.
evals.expected_output: It is email-only: super_login.settings -> super_login.login_type is 2 (0 would be username-or-email, 1 username-only).

evals.prompt: On this site, is the Super Login caps-lock warning currently enabled, and is the username field set to autofocus? Inspect the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: The caps-lock warning is disabled (super_login.capslock = false) and username autofocus is enabled (super_login.autofocus = true).

evals.prompt: Configure Super Login on this site so that users can log in with their email address only, and turn off the Caps Lock warning. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set super_login.settings -> super_login.login_type to 2 (email only) and super_login.capslock to false (e.g. drush cset super_login.settings super_login.login_type 2; drush cset super_login.settings super_login.capslock 0).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site I want the login box to accept only the account username (not the email), and I want the wording above the login form to read exactly: Staff sign in. Make it so on the live site using the Super Login module.
evals.expected_output: Set super_login.settings -> super_login.login_type to 1 (username only) and super_login.login_title to 'Staff sign in'.
